counterfactual_missing_items: A strong, diffuse membranous CD99 pattern that would support Ewing/PNET is not present; observed CD99 is only moderate and patchy.
No renal mass or renal blastemal/epithelial component is present to support Wilms tumor.
Explicit desmoplastic stroma is not stated, but the WT1/CD99 small-round-cell profile is otherwise decisive.
decisive_items: Histopathology showed a multinodular proliferation of small, round, monomorphic cells with clear cytoplasm
Immunohistochemistry demonstrated diffuse strong WT1 positivity and moderate, patchy CD99 positivity
12 cm mass in the anterior superior mediastinum
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete DSRCT answer because it combines the defining raw small-round-cell morphology and strong WT1/moderate-patchy CD99 immunophenotype with the raw anterior-superior-mediastinal mass site. R1 provides the same diagnostic identity but omits the anatomic completion; R4/R3 are CD99-positive small-round-cell alternatives but lack the WT1-driven DSRCT profile; R2 overinterprets isolated WT1 positivity without renal or blastema evidence.

rejected.why: Same correct DSRCT branch but lacks the mediastinal anatomy modifier present in C1.
PNET/Ewing-family small-round-cell alternative with no independent evidence for strong WT1-driven DSRCT; CD99 is not strong/diffuse as typically expected.
Only WT1 positivity is cited; adult/mediastinal Wilms is not supported by the vignette.
